finding: Package engine supports instalment/partial payments, freezing packages for inactive guests, pre-expiry reminders, SMS/OTP identity check at redemption, and cross-location redemption by guest ID.
public_reaction: Indian skin & hair chain case study: saved 16+ hours/month and eliminated manual errors in package tracking.
our_action: Match on package basics (instalments, freeze, expiry nudges, OTP-on-redeem via WhatsApp) since packages drive Indian derma revenue; OTP redemption also stops staff fraud.

finding: Reporting depth is the most-praised area in reviews; Capterra ~4.4/5 (~1,250 reviews), G2 ~4.5/5.
public_reaction: Reviewers often highlight reporting depth; customer service is its highest Capterra sub-score (4.6).
our_action: Ship opinionated clinic KPIs (lead→patient conversion, package liability, doctor/room/machine utilisation, pharmacy margin) out of the box rather than a report builder.

finding: Zenoti dominates Indian beauty/derma chains: Lakmé Salon (300+ salons), plus Kaya Skin, Enrich, O2 Spa and Blush Clinics are cited as Indian clients.
our_action: Don't fight chains head-on at launch; target independent and 1–5 branch derma/hair clinics that are priced out of Zenoti. Use 'chain-grade, clinic-priced' messaging.

finding: In April 2026 Zenoti expanded its 'AI Workforce', including an AI Receptionist that answers calls 24/7 and books, reschedules and confirms appointments; AI is sold as a paid add-on.
our_action: Build an AI layer that lives on WhatsApp (where Indian patients actually enquire): auto-reply to leads, quote package prices within the lowest-price guard, and book slots. Bundle it in the plan instead of upselling it.

finding: Zenoti has a large integrations ecosystem plus native iOS/Android staff (myZen) and white-label client apps; Clinozy is a PWA with only outbound webhooks.
our_action: Short term: a polished installable PWA plus inbound APIs (Meta lead ads, Google, Practo-style listings). Branded patient app later; most Indian patients will use WhatsApp, not an app.

finding: Zenoti includes built-in marketing campaigns, loyalty points and both single and double opt-in for WhatsApp and SMS; Clinozy's brief lists offers but no campaign or loyalty engine.
our_action: Add WhatsApp broadcast campaigns segmented by treatment, recall due and package expiry, plus a simple points/referral wallet.

finding: Pricing is not published and is negotiated through enterprise sales; contracts reportedly run 12–24 months, with an estimated $300–500+/location/month.
public_reaction: Reviewers felt pricing did not match the value received, particularly for single-location or early-stage businesses (per Pabau summary).
our_action: Publish transparent INR pricing per branch on the website, monthly with no lock-in, and a free migration. Message: 'See the price before the demo.'

finding: Cancellation needs written notice (30–90 days in some contracts), there is no self-serve cancel, and early-termination fees apply; some 2025/26 reviews describe billing after cancellation.
public_reaction: Software Finder review (Jan 2026): 'Unauthorized billing after documented cancellation.'
our_action: Offer one-click self-serve cancel and data export (CSV/PDF of patients, photos, ledger). Trust is a selling point when the incumbent traps customers.

finding: Steep learning curve; ease of use is its lowest Capterra sub-score (4.3), and leavers cite too many clicks and screens.
public_reaction: 'Too complicated to use and had problems'; a Reddit user complained of basic tasks taking too many clicks.
our_action: Lead demos with Clinozy's Today floor board and ⌘K palette: 'check-in to checkout in 3 taps'. Measure and publish clicks per common task.

finding: The staff and client mobile apps are reviewed as weaker than desktop, with reports of slowness and glitches after updates.
public_reaction: 'Glitchy' on both home and spa Wi-Fi; 'slow to open client profiles and forms'. App Store reviews mention slow loads after updates.
our_action: Make the PWA fast on mid-range Android over 4G (Indian reality). Target first-load and profile-open times and keep it offline-tolerant.

finding: Some reviewers say support now relies mainly on AI responses, with long waits.
public_reaction: 'Customer service primarily relies on AI responses, resulting in lengthy wait times and a lack of personalized attention.'
our_action: Offer human WhatsApp support in Hindi/English with a named onboarding manager for year one. That is cheap at an early stage and a strong differentiator.

finding: No confirmed native two-way WhatsApp inbox; Indian clinics use third-party connectors (Wati, Onlizer) to bridge WhatsApp to Zenoti.
our_action: Make Clinozy's native WhatsApp lead inbox (Mine/Unreplied views, lead→patient conversion) the headline differentiator against Zenoti in India.

finding: Package freeze plus pre-expiry reminders.
psychology: Loss aversion and the sunk-cost effect: a reminder that 'your 3 remaining laser sessions expire in 14 days' turns prepaid value into a felt loss, which drives rebooking. Freezing preserves the endowment instead of creating resentment.
our_action: Copy, but frame reminders around progress ('you're 4/6 sessions to clear skin') with before/after photos attached. That pairs loss aversion with goal-gradient motivation and avoids sounding like a threat.

finding: Zenoti promotes card-on-file deposits as the most effective way to cut first-rebook cancellations at high-ticket medspas.
psychology: Commitment and loss aversion: a small paid deposit makes the appointment 'mine', and losing it hurts more than the inconvenience of attending.
our_action: India rarely uses cards on file. Use small UPI token deposits via payment links on WhatsApp for laser/PRP/hair-transplant consults, adjustable against the bill so it feels like a pre-payment, not a penalty.

finding: Long contracts plus enterprise-only quotes.
psychology: Lock-in and switching-cost exploitation: high exit friction keeps unhappy customers, but reviews show it breeds resentment that competitors can harvest.
our_action: Use reverse lock-in as a weapon: a 'switch from Zenoti' offer with free data import and months free until the Zenoti contract ends.

finding: Practo owns India's largest doctor-discovery marketplace, and Ray clinic software ties into the Practo.com profile (feedback collection, record sharing, 'My Doctors'), so Ray is bundled with patient acquisition.
our_action: Clinozy can't out-marketplace Practo. Position as owning the clinic's own demand (Instagram/Meta/Google/WhatsApp leads) without per-lead tolls, and ingest Practo bookings via integration where possible.

finding: Low entry price: Ray reportedly starts around ₹999–1,999/month, with bundled SMS (3,000 on CM Atom; 8,000 on Clinic Management).
our_action: Clinozy must stay within reach of a single-doctor derma clinic. Consider a ₹1.5–2.5k/month starter tier with WhatsApp credits included, then upsell pharmacy, stock and multi-branch.

finding: Capterra reviewers praise patient medical history, prescription and treatment-plan modules and easy accounting; G2 4.8 (15 reviews), Capterra 4.0 (8 reviews).
public_reaction: G2 reviewer: comfortable consultation with flexibility in slots; Capterra: the prescription module is good.
our_action: Ensure the derma prescription flow is at least as fast: templates by condition (acne, melasma, alopecia), with WhatsApp delivery of the Rx.

finding: Insta HMS covers pharmacy sales, procurement, stock transfers, consumption tracking and auto-reorder alerts, scaling from single specialty clinics to multi-centre hospitals.
our_action: Clinozy's pharmacy plus MR/supplier module already matches this. Add auto-reorder alerts from the stock runway and expiry-first (FEFO) dispensing to equal Insta.

finding: Practo offers patient-facing discovery, online booking and teleconsult through the Practo app; Clinozy has no consumer channel or public booking page per the brief.
our_action: Build a clinic-branded booking microsite plus a WhatsApp booking link and a Google Business 'Book' integration. Patients book with the clinic, not with a marketplace that shows rival clinics.

finding: Ray's plans bundle SMS, and its plans page does not list WhatsApp, a weak fit for India's WhatsApp-first patients.
our_action: Lead with native two-way WhatsApp (lead inbox, reminders, Rx, invoices, post-care) as the core difference against Practo Ray.

finding: Doctors complain about paid visibility (Practo Prime) and lead packages that underdeliver.
public_reaction: Doctor on Trustpilot: 'paid money to practo for leads that they promised would come'; another reports 'no leads at all'; a 2025 reviewer said Practo promised 3x patients with 'fake charts'.
our_action: Message: 'Your patients, your data, no per-lead tax.' Show lead-source ROI by channel inside Clinozy so clinics can see what Practo leads actually convert to.

finding: Reviews on Practo are seen as unreliable or curated; users allege fake 5-star and suppressed negative reviews, and reviews cannot be edited or deleted.
public_reaction: Trustpilot: 'show all fake and paid 5 stars review'; 'Practo does not publish online negative reviews'.
our_action: Build review requests that route happy patients to the clinic's own Google profile, which the clinic owns. Avoid gating negative feedback; route it privately to a Task for recovery instead.

finding: Support is weak after onboarding; Capterra support score 3.8/5, value 3.9/5.
public_reaction: Google Play doctor review: support is responsive during onboarding but 'getting support is almost impossible' afterward.
our_action: Promise and measure post-onboarding support: WhatsApp support SLA, named CSM, monthly health check.

finding: Ray/Insta are generic multi-specialty tools; there is no evidence of aesthetics-specific features such as before/after photo comparison, laser machine booking or session-based treatment plans.
our_action: Message: 'Built for skin, hair and aesthetics, not for every specialty.' Demo machine scheduling, photo timelines and package sessions; generic tools lack all three.

finding: Practo has faced privacy and data-use scrutiny (HuffPost India report), and doctors worry about a marketplace owning their patient data.
our_action: Make data ownership explicit: DPDP Act-aligned consent, audit log, export anytime, and no patient data shared with any marketplace. Clinozy's MFA and audit log support this message.

finding: Practo Prime paid visibility and ranking.
psychology: Status and FOMO for doctors: ranking higher than peers on Practo signals status, and the fear of competitors outranking them drives renewals even when ROI is unclear.
our_action: Give doctors status the clinic owns: a doctor profile and portfolio page with consented before/after cases and Google reviews, plus a 'top-converting doctor' internal leaderboard, without a pay-to-rank tax.

finding: Marketplace plus software bundle.
psychology: Platform lock-in through the default effect: once the Practo profile is the clinic's main booking source, the bundled Ray software becomes the default, and leaving feels like losing patients.
our_action: Lower the switching cost: import Practo appointments and patients, and keep the Practo profile running alongside Clinozy. Pitch 'keep Practo for discovery, run your clinic on Clinozy.'

finding: Patient reviews on the marketplace.
psychology: Social proof: star ratings strongly influence patient choice, and Practo controls that proof, which gives it leverage over doctors.
our_action: Automate a WhatsApp Google-review request 2 hours after a happy checkout (gated by a feedback-call Task), so social proof accrues to the clinic's own asset.

finding: Aesthetic-specific EMR: digital consent and intake forms sent before the visit and filed to the record, plus integrated before/after photo management and comparison in the Pabau GO app.
public_reaction: Reviewers say it is 'specifically tailored for aesthetic clinics' and 'much more efficient and professional for a busy clinic'.
our_action: Clinozy has photos but no consent/intake forms in the brief. Add procedure-specific digital consent (Hindi/English) with e-signature on tablet or WhatsApp, linked to the treatment session.

finding: Support is consistently the most-praised aspect; Capterra 4.6 (~617 reviews), G2 4.7 (315).
public_reaction: Support team called 'genuinely knowledgeable and proactive, always happy to help with advice or training'.
our_action: Replicate with an onboarding concierge that builds the clinic's services, packages and price list for them during migration.

finding: AI Scribe auto-fills linked consultation forms from the consultation, and AI can build forms from an existing PDF, Word file or photo.
our_action: Build an AI form importer: photograph the clinic's paper consent or case sheet and get a digital form. This removes the biggest setup pain. Add an AI consult-note scribe that supports Hinglish.

finding: Automated pre-care and post-care messaging (instructions sent before and after treatments) is a dedicated Pabau feature; Clinozy's brief has tasks and automation rules but no treatment-linked care journeys.
our_action: Ship treatment-linked WhatsApp care journeys (e.g. 'no sun 48h after peel', day-3 check-in, day-30 rebook) driven by the service catalogue.

finding: Photo consent can be split into separate checkboxes for clinical records and marketing use.
our_action: Add granular photo-consent flags so before/after photos can safely feed marketing; this also helps with DPDP and NMC advertising rules.

finding: Setup is long and complex; building forms and services is described as long-winded, with a big learning curve.
public_reaction: 'Long winded and complicated at times'; 'a lot to learn' but 'gets easier after the initial setup'.
our_action: Offer prebuilt India derma/hair templates (service catalogue, packages, consent, Rx) so a clinic goes live in a day.

finding: Pabau GO launched iOS-first; a reviewer asked for Android availability.
public_reaction: Reviewer wanted Pabau 'available on Android too'.
our_action: India is ~95% Android. Clinozy's PWA must be first-class on Android, with installable home-screen access and camera capture for photos.

finding: Some features are not finished, and the system occasionally glitches.
public_reaction: 'Glitches sometimes'; 'a few features aren't ready that I thought were already functioning'.
our_action: Avoid over-promising in sales; publish a public roadmap and changelog, labelling beta features clearly.

finding: No evidence of a native WhatsApp integration; Pabau is UK/US-centric with SMS/email, and has no GST, Indian pharmacy or INR focus.
our_action: For India, Pabau's aesthetic depth lacks WhatsApp, GST invoices, in-house pharmacy and MR management. Clinozy should claim 'Pabau-grade aesthetics plus Indian clinic operations'.

finding: No free trial or free plan; pricing starts around $59–69/month and scales with users and locations (sources conflict).
our_action: Offer a 14–30 day trial preloaded with demo derma data so owners explore on their own.

finding: Before/after photo comparison in the patient record.
psychology: Progress visibility and goal-gradient effect: seeing visible improvement reinforces the decision to buy (reducing buyer's remorse) and motivates finishing the course. Photos also serve as social proof when consented for marketing.
our_action: Auto-generate side-by-side progress cards at each session and send them on WhatsApp with a 'book next session' button. Make it a habit loop of progress, reward and rebooking.

finding: Pre-care and post-care automated messages.
psychology: Reciprocity and perceived care: unprompted aftercare messages feel like personal attention, building trust and loyalty. They also reduce complications and complaints.
our_action: Send care messages in the doctor's name and language (Hindi/regional) via WhatsApp, with a 'reply if worried' path into the Leads/Conversations inbox.

finding: Digital consent signed before the visit.
psychology: Commitment and consistency: signing in advance is a micro-commitment that raises show-up rates and frames the patient as someone who has already decided.
our_action: Send consent plus a deposit link together on WhatsApp 24h before a procedure, so two micro-commitments stack.

finding: Aesthetics-first HIPAA EMR with charting, before/after photo gallery, inventory, POS and patient communication bundled in all plans; clinical documentation rated strong.
public_reaction: Software Advice reviewer: offers the core features of pricier platforms at a lower cost.
our_action: Benchmark Clinozy's treatment session record against AR: injectables/laser parameters, lot/batch link to stock, photos per session.

finding: Deep brand-loyalty integrations: Evolus Rewards QuickConnect at POS (instant $40 patient savings), Galderma ASPIRE, PatientFi, and RepeatMD membership/rewards (Mar 2025).
our_action: India analogue: integrate pharma/brand schemes and MR programmes (Clinozy already tracks MRs and credits), e.g. track brand-sponsored offers and free samples per patient.

finding: Cherry patient financing is embedded in the POS: enrol patients, check balances and apply payments; practices are paid in 2–3 business days.
our_action: Add a 'pay in EMI' option at checkout via Indian BNPL/EMI partners (card EMI, cardless EMI) for high-ticket packages like hair transplants and laser courses.

finding: Low published entry: about $15–19/user/month plus a $399 one-time onboarding fee and a 14-day trial (practice-reported costs vary widely).
our_action: Low entry pricing wins small clinics; pair it with transparent add-ons so there are no bill surprises.

finding: AR has a Patient Wallet that holds stored credit, rewards and payments per patient; Clinozy has pending credits but no patient-facing wallet.
our_action: Build a patient wallet (advance balance, package credits, referral cash) visible on WhatsApp and the receipt. This turns credits into an endowed asset.

finding: Go-live failures: one clinic could not take bookings for five days after go-live and got poor support follow-up.
public_reaction: Capterra NZ review: failed install, customers 'unable to book for five days' after go-live.
our_action: Offer a zero-downtime migration guarantee: parallel run, import verified before cutover, and a go-live day call.

finding: Reliability complaints: extended outages and bugs during checkout.
public_reaction: 'Kept going down for extended periods'; G2 users hit 'software bugs during checkout'.
our_action: Publish a status page and uptime SLA; checkout must work offline-tolerant (queue payments) for busy Indian front desks.

finding: Low satisfaction overall (Capterra ~3.5/5 from 75 reviews; 60% would recommend) and seen as hard for staff.
public_reaction: 'Time consuming and difficult for staff to use'; chose it as 'the lowest price ... but in the end it did not' work.
our_action: Message to price-sensitive buyers: cheap software that fails costs more. Use role-based simplified views (Therapist, Counsellor), as Clinozy's 'View-as' role preview already shows.

finding: Fewer built-in marketing tools than rivals; a third-party analysis claims the product is in maintenance mode with a single-device login limit.
our_action: Clinozy's Leads CRM plus WhatsApp is a clear edge; stress continuous shipping (changelog).

finding: Switchers to Boulevard cite 'more integrations for marketing, cater more to aesthetics', which shows AR loses on front-of-funnel.
public_reaction: 'Reason for choosing Boulevard: More integrations for marketing, cater more to aesthetics.'
our_action: Combine EMR depth with a lead CRM in one system. That is Clinozy's natural position (Leads plus Patients plus Photos).

finding: Brand reward points (Evolus/ASPIRE) applied instantly at POS.
psychology: Instant gratification and mental accounting: an immediate discount at checkout feels like found money and reduces price pain at the moment of payment, raising acceptance of add-ons.
our_action: At checkout show 'You saved ₹X today (package plus offer)' on the invoice and WhatsApp receipt, and let the lowest-price guard protect margins.

finding: Embedded patient financing (Cherry).
psychology: Pain-of-paying reduction: splitting a large ticket into small instalments lowers the felt cost and anchors on a monthly price, raising conversion on high-value treatments.
our_action: Quote packages as '₹X/month' in counsellor proposals with EMI links; track proposal→paid conversion in Leads.

finding: Patient Wallet holding credits and rewards.
psychology: Endowment effect: money already 'in my wallet at the clinic' feels owned, so patients return to spend it rather than switch clinics.
our_action: Encourage advance top-ups ('add ₹10k, get ₹11k credit') stored in a Clinozy wallet with balance visible on every WhatsApp message.

finding: Premium client-experience booking: card-on-file, deposits and no-show fees up to 100% of service price (some CA spas charge 100% no-show / 50% late cancel), with strong memberships and reporting.
public_reaction: Owner: 'expensive, but ... time is money, and it saved us from a lot of headaches'.
our_action: Copy the deposit/no-show rule engine but in Indian form: UPI token deposits, auto-adjust to the bill, policy text on WhatsApp confirmation.

finding: Memberships are a core growth lever; Boulevard says top membership programmes generate 72% of revenue versus 20% for average ones, and salons with memberships drive 30% more revenue per location.
public_reaction: Medspa owner 'very happy with all of the features, including charting, marketing, patient loyalty, memberships'.
our_action: Add recurring memberships (monthly facial, hydrafacial, laser-hair maintenance) with UPI AutoPay mandates. Clinozy's brief only has packages and offers.

finding: High satisfaction: Capterra 4.6 (364), ease of use 4.6, support 4.7; it raised $80M in 2025 on the Botox/GLP-1 boom.
public_reaction: Praised for 'in-dashboard chat'; 'all-in-one platform that streamlines every aspect of running our MedSpa'.
our_action: Treat polish as a feature: Boulevard wins on UX, so Clinozy's design quality (floor board, ⌘K) must be demo-ready.

finding: Medspa build includes visual charting for injection mapping (Botox and filler face charts) and client profiles with photo galleries.
public_reaction: Reviewers highlight client profiles with notes and photo galleries.
our_action: Add face/scalp diagram charting (injection points, laser zones, hair-graft zones) to treatment sessions.

finding: Enhanced Google integration lets medspa clients book directly from Google Search and Maps.
our_action: Build 'Reserve with Google' or Google Business booking links for Indian clinics, where Google Maps is the top local discovery channel after Instagram.

finding: Boulevard enforces deposits and cancellation fees automatically; Clinozy's brief has bookings by doctor, room and machine but no deposit or no-show policy engine.
our_action: Build deposit rules per service (e.g. laser, PRP, hair transplant consult), with auto-forfeit or credit-to-wallet and a no-show flag on the patient profile.

finding: Expensive: roughly $176–455/location/month (sources vary), with extra charges for additional texts and email tools, a 12-month contract reported, and no free plan or self-serve signup.
public_reaction: Reviewers flag extra charges for additional texts and email tools and full pricing per location.
our_action: Include WhatsApp utility messages (reminders, invoices) in the plan within fair-use, and price multi-branch with a discount rather than full price per location.

finding: Reporting draws criticism despite overall praise.
public_reaction: One reviewer called the reports 'very very bad'.
our_action: Ship reports clinic owners ask for daily: cash close, doctor-wise revenue, package liability, lead conversion. Clinozy already has a daily cash close.

finding: Support channel is limited to text for some users; G2 reviews mention long waits in urgent situations, and there is no staff-to-staff messaging.
public_reaction: 'Texting is only option'; 'long waits for support and difficulty in urgent situations'.
our_action: Offer phone plus WhatsApp support, and add internal staff notes/mentions on patients and tasks (Clinozy Tasks).

finding: EMR is weaker than Aesthetic Record/PatientNow, and one comparison says it lacks built-in consent forms.
our_action: Combine both strengths: Boulevard-grade booking UX with Pabau/AR-grade clinical records, plus pharmacy, which neither has.

finding: Limited customisation for texts and emails; some desired discounts and membership types are unavailable.
public_reaction: 'Certain discounts and memberships that we would like to have aren't available (at this time).'
our_action: Make offers and membership rules flexible (validity, family sharing, branch scope) while keeping the lowest-price guard.

finding: US-only medspa/salon product with no Indian GST invoicing, in-house pharmacy, batch/expiry or MR management.
our_action: Clinozy's Medical room (pharmacy, batches, POs, MRs) is a moat global leaders don't address for Indian derma clinics, which dispense medicines in-house.

finding: No-show fees up to 100% plus card-on-file.
psychology: Loss aversion and pre-commitment: the threat of a charge makes skipping costly, and card-on-file removes the friction of collecting. It can feel punitive and erode goodwill if it is over-applied.
our_action: Frame it positively: 'your ₹500 slot-hold is fully adjusted in your bill'. Allow one free reschedule. That gives fairness and reciprocity without resentment.

finding: Recurring memberships.
psychology: Endowment plus habit loop: monthly benefits that expire ('use it or lose it') create a recurring trigger to book. Membership status creates identity ('I'm a member at X'), and auto-renew relies on status-quo bias.
our_action: Offer 'Glow Club'-style tiers with monthly credits that roll over once (fair), member-only prices shown next to regular prices (anchoring), and UPI AutoPay. Track churn risk when credits go unused.

finding: Client-experience-first booking (luxury feel).
psychology: Halo effect and perceived quality: a premium booking experience signals a premium clinic, which justifies higher prices and builds trust before the visit.
our_action: Give Indian clinics a branded booking page and polished WhatsApp confirmations (doctor photo, map, prep instructions), so a small clinic looks like a chain.
